title: The Six Pillars of Iman
summary: Iman has six pillars that gather the foundations of aqeedah, as the Prophet ﷺ expressed in the hadith of Jibril: to believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and in qadar (divine decree), its good and its bad. Make these for your child the "House of Iman," which has six columns—if they stand firm, the house stands firm. Begin by memorizing them with him in a fun way (counting fingers, a nasheed), then explain each pillar gradually. Do not burden him with details all at once; at this age, it is enough for him to know the six pillars and take pride in being a "believer."
try_this: This week: Memorize the six pillars of Iman with your child by counting them on his fingers every day. The two of you create a drawing of the "House of Iman" and its six columns, and hang it in his room.
reflection_prompts: Why is it preferable to teach the child the general framework (the six pillars) before the details?
How can you make memorizing the pillars an enjoyable experience your child takes pride in, rather than a heavy duty?
